abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) and learning analytics are transforming higher education by enabling personalised learning, adaptive support, and data-informed decision-making. These developments present significant opportunities for improving educational inclusion for students with learning difficulties, yet they also introduce challenges relating to privacy, algorithmic bias, explainability, accessibility, and governance. Although Kuwait has strengthened disability legislation while simultaneously investing in AI-enabled education under Kuwait Vision 2035, these policy agendas have largely evolved independently. abstract: Background Effective communication is fundamental to high-quality healthcare. Communication skills training is a core component of medical curricula, yet opportunities to practice with standardized patients (SPs) are limited, costly, and can elicit anxiety in novice learners. Generative AI (GenAI) virtual patients may offer a scalable and accessible supplement. abstract: Background Sustaining reading motivation in EFL and ESL settings remains a persistent pedagogical challenge. Textbook-based comprehension tasks—with predictable content, pre-printed answer keys, and limited interactivity—can produce passive compliance rather than engagement. The maturation of large-language-model (LLM) tools now makes it feasible for individual practitioners to generate demographically responsive, proficiency-calibrated reading materials at low time cost. title: An analysis of Grade 6 learners’ geometric understanding of rectangles and squares
abstract: Introduction This paper presents an analysis of data collected from 112 Grade 6 learners in Ghana to examine their foundational understanding of two quadrilaterals: squares and rectangles within the NaCCA mathematics curriculum. The study focused on both appearance-based identification and recognition of defining geometric properties. Methods A survey design was employed, and data were gathered using an adapted version of the Van Hiele geometric thinking test. Results The findings show that although learners readily identify squares in familiar orientations, they struggle to recognise rectangles when presented in non-standard forms, demonstrating a strong reliance on prototypical images. Performance on property-based items was consistently low, with correct responses ranging from 7.1% to 26.8%, indicating limited awareness of essential attributes such as parallelism, diagonal congruence, and right-angle bisection. title: Quality assurance 5.0: reframing quality management in higher education through artificial intelligence and continuous institutional learning
abstract: The rapid evolution of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies is fundamentally reshaping higher education, exposing the limitations of conventional quality assurance systems that are often compliance-driven, periodic, and insufficiently responsive to dynamic institutional demands. This conceptual paper introduces Quality Assurance 5.0 (QA 5.0) as a proposed conceptual framework intended to reframe quality management by integrating artificial intelligence, continuous institutional learning, and evidence-informed governance. Drawing on Organisational Learning Theory, Total Quality Management, and Continuous Improvement Theory, the paper synthesises emerging scholarship to propose an adaptive quality ecosystem that is theorised to shift quality assurance from retrospective evaluation to predictive, real-time, and continuous institutional enhancement. title: Beyond technical training: teacher collaboration and informal learning in digital continuing professional development for business studies
abstract: Introduction Teachers' continuous professional development (CPD) is critical for effective digital technology integration in teaching and learning. This study explored how professional development initiatives support Grade 12 Business Studies teachers in integrating digital technologies in resource-constrained rural schools in South Africa. Methods The study adopted a qualitative case study design within the interpretivist paradigm. Data were generated through semi-structured interviews with six purposively sampled Grade 12 Business Studies teachers and analysed thematically. Results The study findings revealed that teachers participated in formal continuous professional development initiatives, including departmental workshops and cluster meetings, as well as informal opportunities such as peer collaboration and self-directed online learning. However, most formal initiatives focused predominantly on technical skills rather than the pedagogical application of digital technologies. Consequently, teachers relied heavily on peer collaboration, professional learning communities and informal digital networks to address gaps in formal training. abstract: Introduction Multimodal language models can inspect submission images directly, potentially bypassing a separate optical-character-recognition pipeline, but end-to-end grading still requires explicit decision rules and a defensible mechanism for human review. title: AI-supported activities for social inclusion: pre-service teachers’ perceptions of opportunities and challenges in special education
abstract: Background Artificial intelligence (AI) has been recognized for enhancing accessibility and learning outcomes for students with disabilities. Nevertheless, very little research has examined the impact of AI on the social inclusion of students with intellectual disabilities, particularly from the perspective of pre-service teachers in authentic practicum contexts. Objective Focusing on student communication, participation, peer interaction, sense of belonging, and implementation conditions, this study investigated pre-service teachers’ perspectives on using AI-supported activities to promote the social inclusion of students with mild-to-moderate intellectual disabilities. abstract: Introduction The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into higher education is transforming how students access learning resources, regulate their learning, and engage in academic activities. However, the mechanisms through which perceived competence in using these technologies relates to students' academic experiences remain insufficiently understood, particularly in the context of language learning. This study aimed to examine whether language learning strategies statistically accounted for an indirect association between AI self-efficacy and satisfaction with studies among Peruvian university students. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted with 254 university students. AI self-efficacy, language learning strategies, and satisfaction with studies were assessed, and their relationships were examined using structural equation modeling (SEM). title: AI-mediated tools in primary English language education: a scoping review of pedagogical functions and teacher orchestration
abstract: AI-mediated tools have expanded from specialised systems to generative and multimodal platforms, but research in primary English language education remains fragmented by technology, educational stage, and evidence type. This scoping review followed JBI methodology and PRISMA-ScR. Scopus, Web of Science Core Collection, and ERIC were searched with a cut-off of 21 September 2026 without publication-year limits. The synthesis included 119 reports, comprising 72 core empirical reports on primary English education, 31 adjacent empirical reports from related settings and 16 contextual sources. The synthesis organised the evidence into five recurring pedagogical functions. These covered oral interaction and speaking rehearsal, pronunciation and oral-reading feedback, and writing, vocabulary, and feedback scaffolding. They also included reading and multimodal meaning-making and teacher-facing assessment and materials design. AI-mediated tools supported structured language practice and feedback-guided activity. title: Responsible student use of generative AI in academic writing: a scoping review of boundaries, educational approaches, and evidence gaps
abstract: Generative AI has complicated how higher education distinguishes assistance from replacement in academic writing, and neither blanket prohibition nor permission resolves it, because the same GenAI-assisted practice may scaffold a student's reasoning or perform the work for students. This scoping review maps how empirical and systematically documented practice-based literature categorises responsible student GenAI use in academic writing, how these boundaries are translated into educational approaches, and what evidence exists for their evaluation and implementation. Following PRISMA-ScR, five databases were searched for English- and Spanish-language higher-education studies published between 1 January 2022 and 6 June 2026, supplemented by citation searching. title: The new constructionism. Papert after Peirce: indexicality, navigational thinking, and learning in the age of generative AI
abstract: The arrival of generative AI in every classroom has produced a crisis that is at once technological, epistemological, and pedagogical. We argue that the appropriate response is neither prohibition nor naive adoption, but a principled reconstruction of constructionism for a computational environment that is generative, context-sensitive, and dialogically accessible. title: Two-tier teaching experiment and third-order modeling
abstract: Constructivist teaching experiments have generated powerful insights into students’ mathematical cognition, but they typically focus on students’ learning in task-based interactions with teacher-researchers and offer only indirect accounts of how teacher-researchers learn from students. To address this limitation, we extend this tradition to a two-tier teaching experiment that explicitly targets teachers’ mathematical learning from student thinking. Grounded in radical constructivism and a perspective on teachers’ mathematical meanings for teaching, we conceptualize teachers’ mathematical meanings of students as teachers’ second-order models of students’ mathematics and position these meanings as constitutive of teachers’ broader mathematical realities. title: Artificial intelligence and universal design for learning in Kuwait’s higher education institutions: towards an AI-enabled framework for inclusive education
abstract: Inclusive education is a strategic priority for higher education institutions worldwide, driven by the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), particularly SDG 4, the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (UNCRPD) and national reform agendas. abstract: Introduction This qualitative meta-synthesis examined the classroom experiences of deaf and hard of hearing (DHH) students in inclusive education settings, with particular attention to communication access and participation. Methods A systematic search of Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus was conducted for peer-reviewed English-language qualitative studies and studies combining qualitative and quantitative methods. Following the screening process, 14 studies (12 qualitative and 2 studies combining qualitative and quantitative methods) were included in the qualitative meta-synthesis. Results The findings were organized into four interconnected themes: factors shaping communication access, classroom participation experiences, social and emotional experiences, and coping and adaptation strategies. Across the included studies, communication access emerged as a central factor influencing students' participation and sense of belonging in inclusive classrooms. abstract: Introduction As artificial intelligence (AI) becomes increasingly embedded in education, it is important to know how confident teachers feel about using it. Research has examined AI literacy, AI readiness and AI competency, yet few validated instruments measure teachers' AI self-efficacy specifically. The aim of this study was to develop and validate the Artificial Intelligence Self-Efficacy Scale for Teachers (AISES-T). Methods Data were collected from teachers in different regions of Turkiye within a scale development design. Following expert review, a pool of 50 items was reduced to a 27-item trial form. title: Socioemotionally responsive teaching in secondary education: teachers’ preparedness, perceptions, and training needs
abstract: Introduction There is currently limited evidence available regarding secondary teachers' preparedness to integrate social and emotional learning explicitly into subject- specific teaching, particularly within the British context examined. This study aimed to analyse the perceived preparedness, self-efficacy, experiences, and training needs of pre-service and in-service secondary teachers regarding the integration of social and emotional learning into teaching practice. Method An explanatory sequential mixed-methods design using the TSEL survey, two open-ended questions, three self-efficacy items, and focus groups for data collection was employed in a convenience sampling of secondary pre-service and in-service teachers in the SouthWest England. title: AI governance readiness as institutional capital: a capability-orchestration framework for student retention intentions in Kazakhstan's higher education
abstract: This study reconceptualizes AI Governance Readiness (AIGR) as a form of institutional capital, representing an institution's capacity to establish, coordinate, and operationalize responsible AI governance arrangements in ways associated with student retention intentions through capability orchestration rather than technology adoption alone. Grounded in the Resource-Based View and Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the study develops and tests a structural model linking AIGR with Administrative Efficiency through AI (AEAI) and AI Fluency Orientation (AIFO), while examining Equity Perception (EPS) as a moderator. title: Can education set the agenda for AI? Simulated innovation and pedagogical direction-setting in teacher education
abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) creates a critical inflection point in the relationship between educational innovation and technological development. For decades, educational systems have often been positioned reactively: technologies emerge, institutions search for their possible pedagogical uses, and teacher education programmes adapt belatedly to tools designed elsewhere. This article argues that GenAI makes this sequence increasingly insufficient. Because GenAI can produce texts, explanations, feedback, learning resources, and assessment artefacts that resemble evidence of educational performance, it compels education to define more clearly what should count as learning, authorship, judgement, and valid evidence. The article develops the concept of simulated innovation to describe technology-led change that signals modernisation without transforming pedagogical purposes, assessment logics, teacher judgement, student agency, or learning relationships. It then argues that GenAI opens the possibility of pedagogical direction-setting: beginning from educational, ethical, epistemic, and democratic aims, and requiring technology to respond to those aims. title: Evaluating a public college's engineering programme: institutional capacity, curriculum responsiveness and employability in the eastern cape, South Africa
abstract: Introduction The rationale and policy governing the establishment of TVET (Technical Vocational Education and Training) colleges clearly state that these institutions must commit to training and student placement, providing them with the necessary competencies for integration into the labour force. Programme offerings are required to be well aligned with the development imperatives of the South African economy and, therefore, enhancing the employability and labour-market integration outcomes within TVET programmes is at the core of their mandate. These envisioned outcomes for TVET institutions are largely dependent on aspects of institutional capacity and the extent to which curricula are responsive to industry requirements. Methods The study evaluated the extent to which a TVET college engineering programme demonstrates curriculum responsiveness and supports employability pathways by examining academic outcomes, institutional capacity, curriculum alignment, stakeholder perceptions, and workforce integration. It employed a convergent mixed-methods research approach to capture the experiences of students, lecturers, and host employers at a TVET college in the Eastern Cape ( n =57).

title: Assessing confidence in scientific-literacy competencies across academic levels in elementary teacher education: a Rasch rating scale analysis
abstract: Introduction Scientific literacy is central to elementary teacher education, but confidence in using scientific-literacy competencies is not equivalent to objectively demonstrated competence and should be measured and interpreted accordingly. This study examined self-reported confidence across four scientific-literacy content domains among elementary teacher-education participants. Methods This cross-sectional study involved 500 participants at Universitas Pendidikan Indonesia, Tasikmalaya Campus (100 each in Years 1–4 and postgraduate study). abstract: Introduction Education for Sustainable Development (ESD) requires primary schools to evaluate not only students' sustainability knowledge and competencies but also the conditions and processes that enable learning and action. However, practical evaluation frameworks linking competence-oriented criteria to evidence-informed school improvement remain limited. This study aimed to develop and refine a school-based evaluation framework for ESD-oriented Comprehensive Practical Activities by integrating Stufflebeam's Context-Input-Process-Product (CIPP) model with the European sustainability competence framework (GreenComp). Methods A mixed-methods action-research study was conducted over two consecutive semesters at an urban primary school in eastern China. title: Advancing sustainability performance through dynamic capabilities and digital transformation: evidence from Saudi higher education institutions
abstract: Introduction Digital transformation is increasingly central to how higher education institutions improve efficiency, accessibility, stakeholder engagement, and sustainability. Yet the organizational capabilities that enable universities to convert digital initiatives into multidimensional sustainability outcomes remain insufficiently differentiated. Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory and the triple-bottom-line perspective, this study examines the direct and indirect relationships of sensing, seizing, learning, and integrating capabilities with sustainability performance through digital transformation in Saudi higher education institutions. Methods Survey data from 215 academic and administrative staff serving as key informants were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. abstract: Introduction The rapid advancement of higher education has significantly influenced various dimensions of student's engagement and teacher's guidance, elicited a need to understand the relationship between them. The collected data were analysed using the mediation analysis for identifying the effects of student aspiration. title: Recurring mechanisms of language use across historical pandemic contexts: evidence from Russian and Polish diasporas in Germany during COVID-19
abstract: This study examines pandemic-affected multilingual practices among Russian and Polish diaspora communities in Germany, situating contemporary empirical findings within a framework of historical evidence on recurrent crisis-induced language use. Drawing on historical research, the study identifies three recurring mechanisms affecting the use of (minoritised) languages: the emergence of new multilingual contact spaces, the temporary expansion of multilingual institutional communication, and the reorganization of language practices within the domestic sphere. Epidemics thus become relevant to language practices through the disruption and reorganization of communicative domains. The empirical analysis focuses on home language use. The dataset consists of semi-structured interviews with Russian- and Polish-speaking migrant families in Germany, reporting on their everyday language practices during the COVID-19 pandemic. title: 21st century honors education in the United States: development, innovation, and best practices
abstract: It is believed that the origins of honors programs in the United States can be traced back to the 1920s, when Swarthmore College in Pennsylvania established one of the first honors programs. Over the years, honors colleges and programs have been established as a means for institutions to recruit the most academically talented students in the country. Since the foundation and inception of honors programs and colleges in the United States, various innovations encompassing both curricular and co-curricular engagement have been established. Unlike non-honors education, honors education offers students more rigorous coursework and higher levels of academic engagement. However, with the looming demographic cliff, increasing competition for students, and decreased funding, challenges persist related to the relevance of honors education in today's generation. Further, honors has been viewed as an exclusive and elitist community of overachievers designed to do overwhelming amounts of additional work. abstract: The rapid pace of technological advancement and the increasing complexity of contemporary educational environments require Initial Teacher Education (ITE) programmes to move beyond the transmission of subject knowledge and pedagogical theory. In this context, combining Virtual Exchange (VE) with Simulation-Based Learning (SBL) offers a promising practice-based approach that bridges theory and practice through intercultural collaboration, experiential learning, and professional role enactment. This study provides context-sensitive evidence on how a VE + SBL model was experienced by Romanian pre-service foreign-language teachers at undergraduate and master's levels. The research design follows a repeated cross-sectional pre-/post-intervention design, with survey data collected from 25 participants at pre-test and 22 at post-test, complemented by qualitative reflections. title: A five-function theory-informed instructional design model for developing clinical reasoning
abstract: Clinical reasoning is an iterative, context-sensitive phenomenon. Its instruction and assessment require distinct forms of educational design. Existing reviews, consensus guidance, and longitudinal curricula provide substantial content and teaching strategies. Further specification is needed to coordinate conceptual preparation, expert modeling, scaffolded whole-case practice, feedback, adaptive fading, and transfer across learner development. We present CRAFT, a theory-informed instructional design model organized around five functions: Conceptualize and Frame, Reveal and Model Clinical Reasoning, Apply Through Scaffolded Practice, Feedback and Reflect, and Transfer Toward Independence. CRAFT provides a curricular architecture organized around proposed readiness gates, in which the five functions recur in progressively more demanding cycles as knowledge, contextual variation, uncertainty, learner responsibility, and assessment stakes increase while instructional support decreases. title: How teachers use Bloom's Taxonomy in the collaborative design of digitally enhanced mathematics lessons: evidence from a PLC-based professional development program
abstract: Introduction The professional development (PD) program examined in this study was structured around school-based professional learning communities (PLCs) to support teachers in integrating digital technologies into mathematics instruction. The PLC model was central to the PD design: although training materials—including videos, demonstrations, and structured tasks—were delivered online through Moodle, the work was implemented within schools, where teachers collaborated in teams. The PD consisted of six sessions distributed across an entire school year, combining the flexibility of online-supported professional learning with the collaborative strength of school-based PLC. abstract: This meta-analysis examined the effect of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) on students' cognitive, learning, and linguistic outcomes.
